output.brief: The jump in DC-stage write-offs is most likely caused by the Phase 2 cut to the night receiving team, not by Haverlow. Since week 31, night pallets have taken a median of about 3 h 52 min to get from unload to chamber, up from 44 min. Staging lanes are unrefrigerated and sit at 15–17°C overnight. Haverlow's trailer telematics, which can't be edited, show loads at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors open. The chambers have held temperature. The warm probe readings were taken hours after unloading, so they show warming on the dock, not warm supply. At night, Haverlow, Pellridge and own-label write-off rates are all about 3%, against about 0.6% by day. That points to the process, not the supplier. Don't raise the chargeback or move volume: it would punish the wrong party. Don't drop the night probe either, because that would hide the problem. Restore six night operatives, or otherwise fix the putaway delay. Set a maximum dock-to-chamber time and track it weekly from scan data. Separately, ask Corriebank for claim-level data to test whether the rise in credits is over-claiming. That part is unproven and I'm much less sure of it. I'm fairly confident about the main cause.
